model.title: A bill to amend the Help America Vote Act of 2002 to require voters to provide photo identification.

summary.text: The bill would require voters to show a valid photo identification to cast a ballot in federal elections. Voters who vote in person and do not show one could still cast a provisional ballot, but it would only count if they show the required identification or an affidavit saying they have a religious objection to being photographed within 3 days. Voters who vote by mail would need to include a copy of a valid photo identification with their ballot, or the last four digits of their Social Security number and an affidavit saying they cannot obtain a copy after reasonable efforts. The bill would also require states to make digital imaging devices available at no cost in public buildings such as courts, libraries, and police stations so people can copy their identification, and to notify new voter registration applicants of the requirement. Accepted forms of identification would include a state driver's license or state ID card with a photo and expiration date, a U.S. passport, a military identification, or a tribal government identification with a photo and expiration date.
